lines.text: Now, timing. A photo is never fresh. It has to be taken, processed, and sent to the robot's brain.
That trip takes a few hundredths of a second, say thirty five thousandths. The robot keeps driving the whole time.
At one point five meters per second, that's about five centimeters of driving.
Draw the tag from where the robot is now, and it lands five centimeters in the wrong place.
So every photo carries its age. And the wheel pose keeps a trail: two hundred fifty dots a second, for one and a half seconds.
We rewind the trail to the moment the photo was taken, stand a ghost robot there, and draw the tag from the ghost. Right on target.
Photos older than a quarter of a second are thrown away. Too stale to trust.
